prompt: An aromatic hydrocarbon shows M⁺ at 92 and a huge peak at m/z = 91 (loss of 1 H). What's happening?

options.label: Benzyl cation forms, then ring-expands to the aromatic tropylium (C₇H₇⁺) — very stable
The molecule loses H₂ (2 Da) to form benzyne, a highly reactive triple-bonded aromatic
Random H loss, with the resulting phenyl-like cation stabilized by aromatic delocalization
H radical loss gives a σ-radical on the ring; the intensity reflects statistical H availability

explanation: Toluene (M=92) loses benzylic H to give benzyl cation (C₆H₅-CH₂⁺) which rapidly rearranges to the TROPYLIUM cation — a 7-membered aromatic ring with 6 π electrons (Hückel aromatic!). Super stabilized → m/z 91 is often the base peak. Diagnostic of alkylbenzenes.
